name: Projected Interpolation Degree
definition: The **projected interpolation degree** is $$\mathrm{intdeg}^p(\mathcal H):=\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal X}\mathrm{intdeg}(\mathcal H_{|S}).$$
description: The largest polynomial interpolation degree required by a coordinate projection.
graph_summary: Maximum interpolation degree over coordinate projections; for finite binary classes it equals VC dimension.

monotonic.proof: For $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, every $\mathcal G_{|S}$ is a subfamily of $\mathcal H_{|S}$, and interpolation degree is subfamily-monotonic. Taking maxima over $S$ preserves the inequality.

p_monotonic.proof: A projection of a projection is a projection of the original class; the set of projections optimized over after projecting is therefore a subset of those optimized over originally.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is a subfamily restriction followed by a projection.

doubly_monotonic.proof: It is both subfamily-monotonic and projection-monotonic by the displayed direct arguments.

strictly_monotonic.proof: For finite binary classes this parameter equals VC dimension. The VC counterexample $\mathcal H=\{000,001,011,100\}$ has both conditioning fibres of value 1 and whole-class value 1, so the strict-C condition fails here as well.
